experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: Synthesis of α-Trifluoromethyl Alcohols and Aldehyde Precursors When Applicable: Representative Procedure for Preparation of α -CF3 Alcohols. Preparation of 2,2,2-Trifluoro-1-(p-tolyl)ethanol23 (2a). The following is a modification of the procedure outlined by Kelly et al.24 To a 100 mL round-bottom flask equipped with a stir bar was added THF (24 mL), p-tolualdehyde (2.723 g, 0.020 mol, 0.83 M, 1 equiv), and (trifluoromethyl)- trimethylsilane (3.12 g, 0.022 mol, 1.3 equiv). The flask was sealed with a rubber septum and placed under a N2 atmosphere via an inlet needle. The reaction mixture was cooled to 0 °C in an ice-water bath and stirred via a magnetic stir plate. After approximately 10 min, TBAF (1 M in THF, 0.2 mL, 0.0002 mol, 0.01 equiv) was added dropwise via a syringe. Note: on small scales, i.e. <20 mmol, the TBAF could be added relatively quickly. However, upon scale-up the addition of TBAF is quite exothermic. Hence, it is recommended that the TBAF be added as slowly as possible and/or the reaction mixture be cooled to a temperature lower than 0 °C. After 10 min, the ice bath was removed and the solution was stirred for approximately 6 h at room temperature. To cleave the silyl ether intermediate, the reaction mixture was cooled to 0 °C in an ice bath. After 10 min, water (2 mL, 0.110 mol, 5.5 equiv) was added via a syringe. TBAF (1 M in THF, 2 mL, 0.002 mol, 0.1 equiv) was then added. After 10 min the ice bath was removed and the reaction mixture was stirred at room temperature. When the cleavage was judged to be complete (determined by GC-MS or NMR), the contents of the flask were transferred to a separatory funnel. Note: some of the silyl ethers were very slow to cleave and required another addition of TBAF and water. Brine (~100mL) and Et2O (~150mL) were added, and the layers were partitioned. The aqueous layer was back-extracted (3 × ~50mL) with Et2O. The combined ether layers were dried with Na2SO4, and the solvent was removed in vacuo via rotary evaporation to afford crude 2, which was further purified by vacuum distillation to give the pure α -CF3 alcohol 2. 1,1,1-Trifluoroundec-10-en-2-ol (2m). The title compound (8.020 g, 92%) was prepared according to the representative procedure from dec-9-enal (6.000 g, 0.0388 mol) followed by vacuum distillation to give the pure α -CF3 alcohol 2m as a clear colorless oil. Aldehyde/ketone (1 mmol) and TMSCF3 (neat) in dry DMF (3 mL) were placed in a 25 mL round-bottom flask (or a 30 mL vial). To this solution was added nucleophilic catalyst, and the mixture was stirred vigorously at room temperature. Completion of the reaction was monitored by TLC and GCMS. experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: General Procedure for the Addition of TMSCF3 to Aldehyde/ Ketone under Nucleophilic Catalysis in DMF. Aldehyde/ketone (1 mmol) and TMSCF3 (neat) in dry DMF (3 mL) were placed in a 25 mL round-bottom flask (or a 30 mL vial). To this solution was added nucleophilic catalyst, and the mixture was stirred vigorously at room temperature. Completion of the reaction was monitored by TLC and GCMS. The reaction mixture was then poured in brine solution (15 mL) and extracted with diethyl ether (3 × 30 mL). Combined organic layers were finally washed with brine solution, dried over anhydrous Na2SO4, and then solvent was removed under reduced pressure. The crude product was further purified by chromatography (using 9:1 hexanes/ethyl acetate solvent system) to afford pure TMS-protected alcohols. A 300 mL, 3-necked, round-bottomed flask was equipped with a gas inlet, septum, stopper and a Teflon-coated stir-bar. The flask was filled with 100 mL of THF and 18.9 mL (18.2 g, 0.128 mol, 1.4 equiv) of TMS-CF3, and the mixture was stirred under an argon atmosphere and cooled to 0 °C in an ice-water bath. Compound 4 (13.0 g, 0.0915 mol) was added via a syringe and the mixture was allowed to stir for five minutes to ensure complete mixing. Tetra-n-butylammonium fluoride (TBAF) (0.92 mL, 0.00092 mol, 1M in THF and 5% w/w. H2O, 0.01 equiv) was then syringed into the mixture, whereupon immediate gas evolution was noted and the solution became an orange color. (Caution: Although not a problem on small scales, when the reaction was performed on this rather large scale, initial gas evolution was such that the stopper had to be held to prevent the flask from opening. If necessary, we suggest cooling the initial mixture further to alleviate this problem.) The orange solution was allowed to warm to room temperature and stir for 30 minutes, whereupon a small aliquot was withdrawn, added to a vial of CH2Cl2 and checked by GC-MS for completeness.a The ketone was seen to be completely converted to the intermediate silyl ether.b In order to cleave the intermediate silyl ether, the flask was placed in an ice-bath for five minutes, and 7.4 mL (0.41 mol, 4.48 equiv) of H2O and an additional 5.0 mL of TBAF solution (0.005 mol, 1M in THF and 5% w/w. H2O, 0.055 equiv) were added via syringe. The flask was removed from the ice-bath and allowed to stir overnight, whereupon GC-MS indicated complete conversion to 7a. Upon completion, approximately 1-2 grams of solid sodium chloride were added to the reaction mixture and it was briefly stirred to assist separation of the THF from the water. Solid NaCl remained in the bottom of the flask. The stirrer was shut off, and the liquid was decanted into a separatory funnel, along with 150 mL of ether, using some of the ether to rinse the salt left in the flask. The mixture was then washed with brine ( 1 X 100 mL), and the two layers separated. The brine layer was back-extracted with additional ether (3 X 25 mL), and these extracts were added to the first organic layer. The combined organic layers were dried with Na2SO4 and gravity-filtered through filter paper into a round bottom flask, using pentane to rinse the Na2SO4. The solvent was removed i n vacuo via rotary evaporation yielding crude 7a as an orange oil. The crude product was purified by vacuum distillationc (bp 78-81 °C @ 30 mm Hg). In order to help prevent solidification of the product in the condenser, a submersible pump in a bucket of 30 °C water was used to circulate water through the condenser. experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: Synthesis of α-Trifluoromethyl Alcohols and Aldehyde Precursors When Applicable: Representative Procedure for Preparation of α -CF3 Alcohols. Preparation of 2,2,2-Trifluoro-1-(p-tolyl)ethanol23 (2a). The following is a modification of the procedure outlined by Kelly et al.24 To a 100 mL round-bottom flask equipped with a stir bar was added THF (24 mL), p-tolualdehyde (2.723 g, 0.020 mol, 0.83 M, 1 equiv), and (trifluoromethyl)- trimethylsilane (3.12 g, 0.022 mol, 1.3 equiv). The flask was sealed with a rubber septum and placed under a N2 atmosphere via an inlet needle. The reaction mixture was cooled to 0 °C in an ice-water bath and stirred via a magnetic stir plate. After approximately 10 min, TBAF (1 M in THF, 0.2 mL, 0.0002 mol, 0.01 equiv) was added dropwise via a syringe. Note: on small scales, i.e. <20 mmol, the TBAF could be added relatively quickly. However, upon scale-up the addition of TBAF is quite exothermic. Hence, it is recommended that the TBAF be added as slowly as possible and/or the reaction mixture be cooled to a temperature lower than 0 °C. After 10 min, the ice bath was removed and the solution was stirred for approximately 6 h at room temperature. To cleave the silyl ether intermediate, the reaction mixture was cooled to 0 °C in an ice bath. After 10 min, water (2 mL, 0.110 mol, 5.5 equiv) was added via a syringe. TBAF (1 M in THF, 2 mL, 0.002 mol, 0.1 equiv) was then added. After 10 min the ice bath was removed and the reaction mixture was stirred at room temperature. When the cleavage was judged to be complete (determined by GC-MS or NMR), the contents of the flask were transferred to a separatory funnel. Note: some of the silyl ethers were very slow to cleave and required another addition of TBAF and water. Brine (~100mL) and Et2O (~150mL) were added, and the layers were partitioned. The aqueous layer was back-extracted (3 × ~50mL) with Et2O. The combined ether layers were dried with Na2SO4, and the solvent was removed in vacuo via rotary evaporation to afford crude 2, which was further purified by vacuum distillation to give the pure α -CF3 alcohol 2. 2,2,2-Trifluoro-1-(4-methoxyphenyl)ethanol28 (2b). experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: Synthesis of α-Trifluoromethyl Alcohols and Aldehyde Precursors When Applicable: Representative Procedure for Preparation of α -CF3 Alcohols. Preparation of 2,2,2-Trifluoro-1-(p-tolyl)ethanol23 (2a). The following is a modification of the procedure outlined by Kelly et al.24 To a 100 mL round-bottom flask equipped with a stir bar was added THF (24 mL), p-tolualdehyde (2.723 g, 0.020 mol, 0.83 M, 1 equiv), and (trifluoromethyl)- trimethylsilane (3.12 g, 0.022 mol, 1.3 equiv). The flask was sealed with a rubber septum and placed under a N2 atmosphere via an inlet needle. The reaction mixture was cooled to 0 °C in an ice-water bath and stirred via a magnetic stir plate. After approximately 10 min, TBAF (1 M in THF, 0.2 mL, 0.0002 mol, 0.01 equiv) was added dropwise via a syringe. Note: on small scales, i.e. <20 mmol, the TBAF could be added relatively quickly. However, upon scale-up the addition of TBAF is quite exothermic. Hence, it is recommended that the TBAF be added as slowly as possible and/or the reaction mixture be cooled to a temperature lower than 0 °C. After 10 min, the ice bath was removed and the solution was stirred for approximately 6 h at room temperature. To cleave the silyl ether intermediate, the reaction mixture was cooled to 0 °C in an ice bath. After 10 min, water (2 mL, 0.110 mol, 5.5 equiv) was added via a syringe. TBAF (1 M in THF, 2 mL, 0.002 mol, 0.1 equiv) was then added. After 10 min the ice bath was removed and the reaction mixture was stirred at room temperature. When the cleavage was judged to be complete (determined by GC-MS or NMR), the contents of the flask were transferred to a separatory funnel. Note: some of the silyl ethers were very slow to cleave and required another addition of TBAF and water. Brine (~100mL) and Et2O (~150mL) were added, and the layers were partitioned. The aqueous layer was back-extracted (3 × ~50mL) with Et2O. The combined ether layers were dried with Na2SO4, and the solvent was removed in vacuo via rotary evaporation to afford crude 2, which was further purified by vacuum distillation to give the pure α -CF3 alcohol 2. 2,2,2-Trifluoro-1-(4-(hydroxymethyl)phenyl)ethanol (2t). experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: General Procedure for the Addition of TMSCF3 to Aldehyde/ Ketone under Nucleophilic Catalysis in DMF. Aldehyde/ketone (1 mmol) and TMSCF3 (neat) in dry DMF (3 mL) were placed in a 25 mL round-bottom flask (or a 30 mL vial). To this solution was added nucleophilic catalyst, and the mixture was stirred vigorously at room temperature. Completion of the reaction was monitored by TLC and GCMS. Combined organic layers were finally washed with brine solution, dried over anhydrous Na2SO4, and then solvent was removed under reduced pressure. A 100 mL, 3-necked, round-bottomed flask was equipped with a gas inlet, a stopper, and a septum. The flask was charged with 5.1 g (0.027 mol 1.28 equiv) of TMS-CF2CF3, 3.0g (0.021 mol, 1 equiv) of 6, and 25 mL of THF. Under argon, the stirred mixture was cooled to 0 °C in an ice-water bath, stirred for 5 minutes, and TBAF (0.22 mL, 0.00022 mol, 1M in THF and 5% w/w. H2O, 0.01 equiv) was then syringed into the mixture, whereupon immediate gas evolution was noted and the solution became a dark brownish-orange color. The ice bath was removed, and the mixture was allowed to warm to room temperature, while stirring. After 3 hours, GC-MS confirmed complete reaction of the starting material to the intermediate silyl ether. In order to cleave the intermediate silyl ether, the flask was placed in an ice-bath for five minutes, and 2.0 mL (0.11 mol, 5.24 equiv) of H2O and an additional 1.3 mL of TBAF solution (0.0013 mol, 1M in THF and 5% w/w. H2O, 0.062 equiv) were added via syringe. The flask was removed from the ice-bath and allowed to stir overnight, whereupon GC-MS indicated complete conversion to 7b. Upon completion, approximately 1 gram of solid sodium chloride was added to the reaction mixture and it was briefly stirred to assist separation of the THF from the water. Solid NaCl remained in the bottom of the flask. The stirrer was shut off, and the liquid was decanted into a separatory funnel, along with 75 mL of ether, using some of the ether to rinse the salt left in the flask. The mixture was then washed with brine ( 1 X 50 mL), and the two layers separated. The brine layer was back-extracted with additional ether (3 X 25 mL), and these extracts were added to the first organic layer. The combined organic layers were dried with Na2SO4 and filtered through filter paper into a round bottom flask, using pentane to rinse the Na2SO4. experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: Typical Experimental Procedure. Tri-tert-butylphosphine [P(t-Bu)3, 3.9 mg, 0.019 mmol]) was placed in a round-bottomed flask under N2. experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: Typical Procedure for Trifluoromethylation of Various Nitriles Promoted by TBABF. Biphenyl-4-carbonitrile (110 mg, 0.61 mmol) was dissolved in THF (4 mL). Under nitrogen at 0 °C (trifluoromethyl)trimethylsilane (0.45 mL, 3.05 mmol, 5 equiv) was added. To this mixture was then added TBAF•HF (0.360 g, 1.28 mmol, 2.1 equiv) solution in THF (4 mL). The cooling bath was removed, and the reaction mixture was stirred at 25 °C for 2 h. The reaction mixture was concentrated under rotary vacuum to give a light yellow gum. Column chromatography of the residue (silica gel, hexane-EtOAc = 5:1) provided 2-biphenyl-4-yl-1,1,1,3,3,3-hexafluoropropan-2-amine. 2-Naphthylaldehyde and 2'-acetonaphthone reacted in the presence of TMSCF3 and a catalytic amount of TBABF to provide the desired trifluoromethyl alcohols in 95% and 92% yields, respectively. Yield 92%.

experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: Synthesis of α-Trifluoromethyl Alcohols and Aldehyde Precursors When Applicable: Representative Procedure for Preparation of α -CF3 Alcohols. Preparation of 2,2,2-Trifluoro-1-(p-tolyl)ethanol23 (2a). The following is a modification of the procedure outlined by Kelly et al.24 To a 100 mL round-bottom flask equipped with a stir bar was added THF (24 mL), p-tolualdehyde (2.723 g, 0.020 mol, 0.83 M, 1 equiv), and (trifluoromethyl)- trimethylsilane (3.12 g, 0.022 mol, 1.3 equiv). The flask was sealed with a rubber septum and placed under a N2 atmosphere via an inlet needle. The reaction mixture was cooled to 0 °C in an ice-water bath and stirred via a magnetic stir plate. After approximately 10 min, TBAF (1 M in THF, 0.2 mL, 0.0002 mol, 0.01 equiv) was added dropwise via a syringe. Note: on small scales, i.e. <20 mmol, the TBAF could be added relatively quickly. However, upon scale-up the addition of TBAF is quite exothermic. Hence, it is recommended that the TBAF be added as slowly as possible and/or the reaction mixture be cooled to a temperature lower than 0 °C. After 10 min, the ice bath was removed and the solution was stirred for approximately 6 h at room temperature. To cleave the silyl ether intermediate, the reaction mixture was cooled to 0 °C in an ice bath. After 10 min, water (2 mL, 0.110 mol, 5.5 equiv) was added via a syringe. TBAF (1 M in THF, 2 mL, 0.002 mol, 0.1 equiv) was then added. After 10 min the ice bath was removed and the reaction mixture was stirred at room temperature. When the cleavage was judged to be complete (determined by GC-MS or NMR), the contents of the flask were transferred to a separatory funnel. Note: some of the silyl ethers were very slow to cleave and required another addition of TBAF and water. Brine (~100mL) and Et2O (~150mL) were added, and the layers were partitioned. The aqueous layer was back-extracted (3 × ~50mL) with Et2O. The combined ether layers were dried with Na2SO4, and the solvent was removed in vacuo via rotary evaporation to afford crude 2, which was further purified by vacuum distillation to give the pure α -CF3 alcohol 2. 2,2,2-Trifluoro-1-(2-nitrophenyl)ethanol28 (2j). The title compound (3.340 g, 76%) was prepared according to the representative procedure from o-nitrobenzaldehyde (3.020 g, 0.020 mol) followed by vacuum distillation to give the pure α- CF3 alcohol 2j as a clear yellow oil. The following is a modification of the procedure outlined by Kelly et al.24 To a 100 mL round-bottom flask equipped with a stir bar was added THF (24 mL), p-tolualdehyde (2.723 g, 0.020 mol, 0.83 M, 1 equiv), and (trifluoromethyl)- trimethylsilane (3.12 g, 0.022 mol, 1.3 equiv). The flask was sealed with a rubber septum and placed under a N2 atmosphere via an inlet needle. The reaction mixture was cooled to 0 °C in an ice-water bath and stirred via a magnetic stir plate. After approximately 10 min, TBAF (1 M in THF, 0.2 mL, 0.0002 mol, 0.01 equiv) was added dropwise via a syringe. Note: on small scales, i.e. <20 mmol, the TBAF could be added relatively quickly. However, upon scale-up the addition of TBAF is quite exothermic. Hence, it is recommended that the TBAF be added as slowly as possible and/or the reaction mixture be cooled to a temperature lower than 0 °C. After 10 min, the ice bath was removed and the solution was stirred for approximately 6 h at room temperature. To cleave the silyl ether intermediate, the reaction mixture was cooled to 0 °C in an ice bath. After 10 min, water (2 mL, 0.110 mol, 5.5 equiv) was added via a syringe. TBAF (1 M in THF, 2 mL, 0.002 mol, 0.1 equiv) was then added. After 10 min the ice bath was removed and the reaction mixture was stirred at room temperature. When the cleavage was judged to be complete (determined by GC-MS or NMR), the contents of the flask were transferred to a separatory funnel. Note: some of the silyl ethers were very slow to cleave and required another addition of TBAF and water. Brine (~100mL) and Et2O (~150mL) were added, and the layers were partitioned. The aqueous layer was back-extracted (3 × ~50mL) with Et2O. The combined ether layers were dried with Na2SO4, and the solvent was removed in vacuo via rotary evaporation to afford crude 2, which was further purified by vacuum distillation to give the pure α -CF3 alcohol 2. 3-Cyclohexyl-1,1,1-trifluoropropan-2-ol (2n). The following is a modification of the procedure outlined by Kelly et al.24 To a 100 mL round-bottom flask equipped with a stir bar was added THF (24 mL), p-tolualdehyde (2.723 g, 0.020 mol, 0.83 M, 1 equiv), and (trifluoromethyl)- trimethylsilane (3.12 g, 0.022 mol, 1.3 equiv). The flask was sealed with a rubber septum and placed under a N2 atmosphere via an inlet needle. The reaction mixture was cooled to 0 °C in an ice-water bath and stirred via a magnetic stir plate. After approximately 10 min, TBAF (1 M in THF, 0.2 mL, 0.0002 mol, 0.01 equiv) was added dropwise via a syringe. Note: on small scales, i.e. <20 mmol, the TBAF could be added relatively quickly. However, upon scale-up the addition of TBAF is quite exothermic. Hence, it is recommended that the TBAF be added as slowly as possible and/or the reaction mixture be cooled to a temperature lower than 0 °C. After 10 min, the ice bath was removed and the solution was stirred for approximately 6 h at room temperature. To cleave the silyl ether intermediate, the reaction mixture was cooled to 0 °C in an ice bath. After 10 min, water (2 mL, 0.110 mol, 5.5 equiv) was added via a syringe. TBAF (1 M in THF, 2 mL, 0.002 mol, 0.1 equiv) was then added. After 10 min the ice bath was removed and the reaction mixture was stirred at room temperature. When the cleavage was judged to be complete (determined by GC-MS or NMR), the contents of the flask were transferred to a separatory funnel. Note: some of the silyl ethers were very slow to cleave and required another addition of TBAF and water. Brine (~100mL) and Et2O (~150mL) were added, and the layers were partitioned. The aqueous layer was back-extracted (3 × ~50mL) with Et2O. The combined ether layers were dried with Na2SO4, and the solvent was removed in vacuo via rotary evaporation to afford crude 2, which was further purified by vacuum distillation to give the pure α -CF3 alcohol 2. 2,2,2-Trifluoro-1-(3-methoxyphenyl)ethanol (2c). The title compound (3.405 g, 83%) was prepared according to the representative procedure from m-anisaldehyde (2.723 g, 0.020 mol) followed by vacuum distillation to give the pure α- CF3 alcohol 2c as a clear colorless oil. experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: Synthesis of α-Trifluoromethyl Alcohols and Aldehyde Precursors When Applicable: Representative Procedure for Preparation of α -CF3 Alcohols. Preparation of 2,2,2-Trifluoro-1-(p-tolyl)ethanol23 (2a). The following is a modification of the procedure outlined by Kelly et al.24 To a 100 mL round-bottom flask equipped with a stir bar was added THF (24 mL), p-tolualdehyde (2.723 g, 0.020 mol, 0.83 M, 1 equiv), and (trifluoromethyl)- trimethylsilane (3.12 g, 0.022 mol, 1.3 equiv). The flask was sealed with a rubber septum and placed under a N2 atmosphere via an inlet needle. The reaction mixture was cooled to 0 °C in an ice-water bath and stirred via a magnetic stir plate. After approximately 10 min, TBAF (1 M in THF, 0.2 mL, 0.0002 mol, 0.01 equiv) was added dropwise via a syringe. Note: on small scales, i.e. <20 mmol, the TBAF could be added relatively quickly. However, upon scale-up the addition of TBAF is quite exothermic. Hence, it is recommended that the TBAF be added as slowly as possible and/or the reaction mixture be cooled to a temperature lower than 0 °C. After 10 min, the ice bath was removed and the solution was stirred for approximately 6 h at room temperature. To cleave the silyl ether intermediate, the reaction mixture was cooled to 0 °C in an ice bath. After 10 min, water (2 mL, 0.110 mol, 5.5 equiv) was added via a syringe. TBAF (1 M in THF, 2 mL, 0.002 mol, 0.1 equiv) was then added. After 10 min the ice bath was removed and the reaction mixture was stirred at room temperature. When the cleavage was judged to be complete (determined by GC-MS or NMR), the contents of the flask were transferred to a separatory funnel. Note: some of the silyl ethers were very slow to cleave and required another addition of TBAF and water. Brine (~100mL) and Et2O (~150mL) were added, and the layers were partitioned. The aqueous layer was back-extracted (3 × ~50mL) with Et2O. The combined ether layers were dried with Na2SO4, and the solvent was removed in vacuo via rotary evaporation to afford crude 2, which was further purified by vacuum distillation to give the pure α -CF3 alcohol 2. 2,2,2-Trifluoro-1-(pyridin-2-yl)ethanol29 (2k). The title compound (2.920 g, 82%) was prepared according to the representative procedure from picolinaldehyde (2.142 g, 0.020 mol) followed by vacuum distillation to give the pure α- CF3 alcohol 2k as a clear colorless oil. Aldehyde/ketone (1 mmol) and TMSCF3 (neat) in dry DMF (3 mL) were placed in a 25 mL round-bottom flask (or a 30 mL vial). To this solution was added nucleophilic catalyst, and the mixture was stirred vigorously at room temperature. Completion of the reaction was monitored by TLC and GCMS. The flask was sealed with a rubber septum and placed under a N2 atmosphere via an inlet needle. The reaction mixture was cooled to 0 °C in an ice-water bath and stirred via a magnetic stir plate. After approximately 10 min, TBAF (1 M in THF, 0.2 mL, 0.0002 mol, 0.01 equiv) was added dropwise via a syringe. Note: on small scales, i.e. <20 mmol, the TBAF could be added relatively quickly. However, upon scale-up the addition of TBAF is quite exothermic. Hence, it is recommended that the TBAF be added as slowly as possible and/or the reaction mixture be cooled to a temperature lower than 0 °C. After 10 min, the ice bath was removed and the solution was stirred for approximately 6 h at room temperature. To cleave the silyl ether intermediate, the reaction mixture was cooled to 0 °C in an ice bath. After 10 min, water (2 mL, 0.110 mol, 5.5 equiv) was added via a syringe. TBAF (1 M in THF, 2 mL, 0.002 mol, 0.1 equiv) was then added. After 10 min the ice bath was removed and the reaction mixture was stirred at room temperature. experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: General Procedures for the Trifluoromethylation of N-Benzoylaldohydrazones. Method A. Allyltrimethylsilane (166 μL, 1.05 mmol) and BF3 · OEt2 (133 μL, 1.05 mmol) were successively added to a suspension of N-bezoylhydrazone (0.7 mmol) in 1,2-dichloroethane (1.4 mL), and the mixture was heated at gentle reflux for 5 min. The solvent was evaporated in vacuum, the residue was dissolved in DMF (1.4 mL) followed by addition of Me3SiCF3 (207 μL, 1.4 mmol) and NaOAc (230 mg, 2.8 mmol). The mixture was stirred for 2 h at room temperature, quenched with 1 mL of saturated aqueous Na2CO3, and stirred for additional 5 min. The mixture was diluted with water (~10 mL) and extracted with ether (for 3a-c,e,g-k) or ethyl acetate (for 3d,f) (4 × 4 mL). The combined organic phase was dried with Na2SO4, concentrated, and the residue was flash chromatographed on silica gel. N'-[2,2,2-trifluoro-1-(4-nitrophenyl)ethyl]benzohydrazide (3d). Chromatography: hexanes/EtOAc, 2 : 1, Rf = 0.28 (hexanes/EtOAc, 3 : 1). experimental_procedure: In a flask was dissolved 2-methoxy-4-nitrobenzaldehye (9.93 g, 54.8 mmol) in anhydrous DME (100 mL), and the mixture was stirred to obtain a clear yellow solution. experimental_procedure: General Procedures for the Trifluoromethylation of N-Benzoylaldohydrazones. Method A. experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: General procedure for the enantioselective trifluoromethylation reaction of alkynyl ketones : To a stirred solution of alkynyl ketone 1 (0.20 mmol), catalyst 3a (17.0 mg, 0.020 mmol, 10 mol%) and Me4NF (3.7 mg, 0.040 mmol, 0.2 equiv) in toluene/CH2Cl2 (2/1, 0.5 mL) was added Me3SiCF3 (59.1 μL, 0.40 mmol, 2.0 equiv) at −60°C under nitrogen atmosphere. Aldehyde/ketone (1 mmol) and TMSCF3 (neat) in dry DMF (3 mL) were placed in a 25 mL round-bottom flask (or a 30 mL vial). experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: Synthesis of α-Trifluoromethyl Alcohols and Aldehyde Precursors When Applicable: Representative Procedure for Preparation of α -CF3 Alcohols. Preparation of 2,2,2-Trifluoro-1-(p-tolyl)ethanol23 (2a). The following is a modification of the procedure outlined by Kelly et al.24 To a 100 mL round-bottom flask equipped with a stir bar was added THF (24 mL), p-tolualdehyde (2.723 g, 0.020 mol, 0.83 M, 1 equiv), and (trifluoromethyl)- trimethylsilane (3.12 g, 0.022 mol, 1.3 equiv). The flask was sealed with a rubber septum and placed under a N2 atmosphere via an inlet needle. The reaction mixture was cooled to 0 °C in an ice-water bath and stirred via a magnetic stir plate. After approximately 10 min, TBAF (1 M in THF, 0.2 mL, 0.0002 mol, 0.01 equiv) was added dropwise via a syringe. Note: on small scales, i.e. <20 mmol, the TBAF could be added relatively quickly. However, upon scale-up the addition of TBAF is quite exothermic. Hence, it is recommended that the TBAF be added as slowly as possible and/or the reaction mixture be cooled to a temperature lower than 0 °C. After 10 min, the ice bath was removed and the solution was stirred for approximately 6 h at room temperature. To cleave the silyl ether intermediate, the reaction mixture was cooled to 0 °C in an ice bath. After 10 min, water (2 mL, 0.110 mol, 5.5 equiv) was added via a syringe. TBAF (1 M in THF, 2 mL, 0.002 mol, 0.1 equiv) was then added. After 10 min the ice bath was removed and the reaction mixture was stirred at room temperature. When the cleavage was judged to be complete (determined by GC-MS or NMR), the contents of the flask were transferred to a separatory funnel. Note: some of the silyl ethers were very slow to cleave and required another addition of TBAF and water. Brine (~100mL) and Et2O (~150mL) were added, and the layers were partitioned. The aqueous layer was back-extracted (3 × ~50mL) with Et2O. The combined ether layers were dried with Na2SO4, and the solvent was removed in vacuo via rotary evaporation to afford crude 2, which was further purified by vacuum distillation to give the pure α -CF3 alcohol 2. 2,2,2-Trifluoro-1-(2-methoxyphenyl)ethanol (2i). The title compound (3.520 g, 85%) was prepared according to the representative procedure from o-methoxybenzaldehyde (2.720 g, 0.020 mol) followed by vacuum distillation to give the pure α -CF3 alcohol 2i as a clear colorless oil. TBAF (1 M in THF, 2 mL, 0.002 mol, 0.1 equiv) was then added. After 10 min the ice bath was removed and the reaction mixture was stirred at room temperature. experimental_procedure: Synthesis of α-Trifluoromethyl Alcohols and Aldehyde Precursors When Applicable: Representative Procedure for Preparation of α -CF3 Alcohols. Preparation of 2,2,2-Trifluoro-1-(p-tolyl)ethanol23 (2a). The following is a modification of the procedure outlined by Kelly et al.24 To a 100 mL round-bottom flask equipped with a stir bar was added THF (24 mL), p-tolualdehyde (2.723 g, 0.020 mol, 0.83 M, 1 equiv), and (trifluoromethyl)- trimethylsilane (3.12 g, 0.022 mol, 1.3 equiv). The flask was sealed with a rubber septum and placed under a N2 atmosphere via an inlet needle. The reaction mixture was cooled to 0 °C in an ice-water bath and stirred via a magnetic stir plate. After approximately 10 min, TBAF (1 M in THF, 0.2 mL, 0.0002 mol, 0.01 equiv) was added dropwise via a syringe. Note: on small scales, i.e. <20 mmol, the TBAF could be added relatively quickly. However, upon scale-up the addition of TBAF is quite exothermic. Hence, it is recommended that the TBAF be added as slowly as possible and/or the reaction mixture be cooled to a temperature lower than 0 °C. After 10 min, the ice bath was removed and the solution was stirred for approximately 6 h at room temperature. To cleave the silyl ether intermediate, the reaction mixture was cooled to 0 °C in an ice bath. After 10 min, water (2 mL, 0.110 mol, 5.5 equiv) was added via a syringe. TBAF (1 M in THF, 2 mL, 0.002 mol, 0.1 equiv) was then added. After 10 min the ice bath was removed and the reaction mixture was stirred at room temperature. When the cleavage was judged to be complete (determined by GC-MS or NMR), the contents of the flask were transferred to a separatory funnel. Note: some of the silyl ethers were very slow to cleave and required another addition of TBAF and water. Brine (~100mL) and Et2O (~150mL) were added, and the layers were partitioned. The aqueous layer was back-extracted (3 × ~50mL) with Et2O. The combined ether layers were dried with Na2SO4, and the solvent was removed in vacuo via rotary evaporation to afford crude 2, which was further purified by vacuum distillation to give the pure α -CF3 alcohol 2. 2,2,2-Trifluoro-1-(p-tolyl)ethanol25 (2a). The title compound (3.02 g, 79%) was prepared according to the representative procedure from p-tolualdehyde (2.723 g, 0.020 mol) followed by vacuum distillation to give the pure α -CF3 alcohol 2a as a colorless oil. Hence, it is recommended that the TBAF be added as slowly as possible and/or the reaction mixture be cooled to a temperature lower than 0 °C.
